fullPassage:
[1번] In a scientific study, 72 people were asked to listen to "dad jokes." After each joke, there was either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter. The participants then rated how funny the jokes were. Jokes with no laughter didn't get high ratings. Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated 10 percent funnier. And jokes followed by real laughter were rated 20 percent funnier. This study shows that both real and fake laughter make a big difference in how funny we find jokes. It suggests that we pay close attention not just to a joke's content but also to the reaction it gets. This is because we get ready to smile or laugh when we hear someone else laughing. Essentially, laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also brings people together. This highlights laughter's social and contagious nature.

[2번] Music sampling involves taking part of an existing recording and using it in a new song. Musicians have been sampling for a long time, but the practice has become more common in recent years. Samples from older songs are often used to bring back old memories. By using samples that are familiar to older listeners, musicians create music that is popular with people of all ages. Musicians use samples not only to bridge generation gaps between listeners, but also to create new approaches to song production. They want to create unique sounds and come up with innovative ways of writing songs. Therefore, we can expect to see new and experimental ways of including samples in songs, and for sampling to become more and more popular in the future.

[3번] There will soon be many self-driving cars with internet access on the road. Although these cars have many benefits, experts warn that having more self-driving cars also means having more potential targets for hackers. Researchers recently proved through a demonstration that even today's "smart" cars are vulnerable. They used a computer to take control of a car while someone else was driving it. They were not only able to change the radio's volume, adjust the air conditioner, and switch the windshield wipers on, but they were also able to take control of the transmission and stop the car as it was driving down the highway. Fortunately, it was just a demonstration, but it sends a clear message to both the auto industry and the government: automotive cybersecurity is a real issue that must be taken seriously.

[4번] The "sharing economy" is a system based on the idea of individuals renting things from each other through the internet. Things now commonly rented in this way include houses, cars, boats, and power tools. These items are considered by many to be too expensive to own but are owned by others who are willing to share them for a price. This collaborative use of resources has several positive effects. Owners make money from the things they own, and renters pay less than they would if they bought the things themselves or rented them from a company such as a car rental agency. The environment also benefits because sharing a product with others rather than buying the product for yourself means fewer resources are consumed in making products. As more people use sharing services, these benefits are likely to grow.

[5번] Astronauts feel weightless when they travel outside our planet's atmosphere because the speed of a spacecraft in orbit balances the force of Earth's gravitational pull. In fact, you may have experienced a similar feeling when riding a roller coaster. As the roller coaster car climbs up the track, gravity pulls your body downward, and you feel yourself pushed down on your seat. However, when the car rushes down, your body hangs in the air until it is pulled down by your safety belt. Using this phenomenon, NASA prepares its astronauts for space travel. The astronauts fly in an aircraft that ascends to an altitude of 24,000 feet, and once the aircraft dives down, the passengers experience about 20 to 25 seconds of weightlessness. These flights help astronauts get used to the environment of space, and they allow NASA to conduct experiments and test equipment in a similar environment as well.

[6번] In order to efficiently process information, our brains employ strategies that affect how we gather and interpret data. One of these strategies is called confirmation bias, and it occurs when we interpret information in a way that supports what we already believe. A study from Stanford University in 1979 revealed how powerful confirmation bias is. Researchers produced two fake research reports with opposing arguments about the effects of capital punishment. One of the reports suggested that capital punishment leads to reduced crime rates, while the other proposed that the two were not related. When participants were presented with these fabricated reports, their responses were shown to be significantly influenced by their existing opinions on the issue. Even when they encountered evidence that contradicted their beliefs, the impact of confirmation bias proved to be highly significant.

[7번] While you're unlikely to receive an email from a vegetable, it's not impossible. A team of engineers placed special devices in spinach plants that emit a signal when they sense nitroaromatic compounds in the soil. These components are commonly found in explosives. The signal causes a small computer to send an email to the engineers. The goal of this study was to find out if spinach could detect explosives, but the technology involved has broader potential. It is possible that it can be used to help scientists gather vital information about environmental conditions. The engineers believe plants have the ability to predict upcoming droughts, as well as more subtle changes in soil and water, as they grow. They could also be useful in detecting pollution and combating climate change.

[8번] To tantalize someone is to make them want something, often something they can never get. The word comes from the Greek myth of King Tantalus, who was so proud that he tried to fool the gods. When invited to eat with them, Tantalus stole their special food so that he could bring it to his friends. As a punishment, he was sent to the underworld. He had to stand in a pool of water with delicious ripe fruit hanging from a tree above him. Whenever he tried to drink the water, it would drain away. If he tried to pick the fruit, the branches would move out of reach. Tantalus was already in the underworld, so no matter how hungry or thirsty he got, he would never die.

det.korean: ① to take → taking: 동사 involve는 뒤에 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로 taking이 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① to take — 원문은 taking이에요. 동사 involve(~을 수반하다)는 뒤에 동사가 올 때 -ing형(동명사)을 목적어로 써요. 'involves taking part(일부를 가져오는 것을 수반한다)'가 맞고, to부정사 to take는 쓸 수 없어 틀려요 ←정답

❌ ② to bring — 'are often used to bring back(되살리기 위해 사용된다)'에서 '~하기 위해'라는 목적의 to부정사로 정상이에요.

❌ ③ is popular — 관계대명사 that이 앞의 'music(음악)'을 가리키는데 music은 단수라 is로 정상이에요. 바로 앞 people 때문에 are로 착각하기 쉽지만 that이 가리키는 것은 music이에요.

One of the reports suggested that capital punishment leads to reduced crime rates, while the other proposed that the two were not related. When participants were presented with these fabricated reports, their responses were shown to be significantly influenced by their __________ on the issue. Even when they encountered evidence that contradicted their beliefs, the impact of confirmation bias proved to be highly significant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: research reports=연구 보고서 / reduced rates=줄어든 비율 / fake arguments=가짜 주장 / existing opinions=기존 의견
det.analysis:
① research reports: 보고서에 대한 영향? 문맥 부적절
② reduced rates: 줄어든 비율? 부적절
③ fake arguments: 가짜 주장? 부적절
④ existing opinions: 그 사안에 대한 기존 의견의 영향을 크게 받음 ←정답
det.tip: influenced by their ______ on the issue → 기존 의견(existing opinions)

questions.passage: While you're unlikely to receive an email from a vegetable, it's not impossible. A team of engineers placed special devices in spinach plants that emit a signal when they sense nitroaromatic compounds in the soil. These components are commonly found in explosives. The signal causes a small computer to send an email to the engineers. The goal of this study was to find out if spinach could detect explosives, but the technology involved has __________. It is possible that it can be used to help scientists gather vital information about environmental conditions. The engineers believe plants have the ability to predict upcoming droughts, as well as more subtle changes in soil and water, as they grow. They could also be useful in detecting pollution and combating climate change.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 앞 'but(그러나)'이 대조 신호다. 원래 목표는 폭발물 탐지였지만 그 기술은 '더 넓은 잠재력(broader potential)'을 지닌다는 흐름이다.
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 'The goal of this study was to find out if spinach could detect explosives, but the technology involved has __________(이 연구의 목표는 시금치가 폭발물을 감지할 수 있는지 알아내는 것이었지만, 그 기술은 __________을 지닌다)'예요. 접속사 but 뒤라서 '원래의 좁은 목표'와 대조되는 '더 넓은 가능성'이 들어가야 해요. 뒤이어 환경 정보 수집, 오염 감지 등 다양한 쓰임이 이어지죠.

✅ ① broader potential(더 넓은 잠재력) — 원래 목표를 넘어선 폭넓은 활용 가능성이라 흐름과 딱 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ② a single use(단 하나의 용도) — 뒤에 여러 활용이 나오므로 '하나의 용도'는 반대예요.

❌ ③ serious risks(심각한 위험) — 위험을 경고하는 글이 아니에요.

❌ ④ little value(거의 없는 가치) — 오히려 가치가 크다고 말하는 글이라 반대예요.
det.tip: but(그러나) 뒤 대조 + 이어지는 다양한 활용 → broader potential(더 넓은 잠재력)

questions.passage: To tantalize someone is to make them want something, often something they can never get. The word comes from the Greek myth of King Tantalus, who was so proud that he tried to ①<u>fool</u> the gods. When invited to eat with them, Tantalus stole their special food so that he could bring it to his friends. As a punishment, he was ②<u>sent</u> to the underworld. He had to stand in a pool of water with delicious ripe fruit ③<u>hangs</u> from a tree above him. Whenever he tried to ④<u>drink</u> the water, it would drain away. If he tried to pick the fruit, the branches would move out of reach. Tantalus was already in the underworld, so no matter how hungry or thirsty he got, he would never die.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: hangs → hanging ('with + 명사 + 분사' 구문에서는 완전한 동사가 아니라 분사)
det.analysis:
① fool: 'tried to fool' to부정사 뒤 동사원형 — 적절

② sent: 'he was sent' be동사 + 과거분사(수동태) — 적절

③ hangs: 'with delicious ripe fruit hangs from a tree'? 'with + 명사 + 분사'는 '~한 채'라는 부대상황을 나타내는데, 여기서는 완전한 동사(hangs)가 아니라 분사가 와야 해요. 과일이 스스로 매달린 능동이라 현재분사 hanging → hanging ←정답

④ drink: 'tried to drink' to부정사 뒤 동사원형 — 적절
det.tip: with + 명사 + 분사. 과일이 매달린 능동 → hanging

questions.passage: In a ①<u>scientific</u> study, 72 people were asked to listen to "dad jokes." After each joke, there was either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter. The participants then rated how funny the jokes were. Jokes with no laughter didn't get ②<u>low ratings</u>. Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated 10 percent funnier. And jokes followed by real laughter were rated 20 percent funnier. This study shows that both real and fake laughter make a big difference in how funny we find jokes. It suggests that we pay ③<u>close</u> attention not just to a joke's content but also to the reaction it gets. This is because we get ready to smile or laugh when we hear someone else laughing. Essentially, laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also brings people ④<u>together</u>. This highlights laughter's social and contagious nature.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② low → high. 웃음이 없는 농담은 '높은' 평가를 받지 못했다는 흐름이므로 high ratings
det.analysis:
① scientific: 과학적인 연구 — 적절

② low: 웃음이 없는 농담이 '낮은' 평가를 못 받았다? 뒤에 웃음이 있으면 더 웃기게 평가된다는 흐름상 원래 못 받은 것은 '높은' 평가 → high가 맞음 ←정답

③ close: 'pay close attention' 세심한 주의 — 적절

④ together: 사람들을 하나로 모음 — 적절
det.tip: no laughter → didn't get high ratings(높은 평가를 못 받음). low는 문맥상 반대

questions.passage: Music sampling ①<u>involves</u> taking part of an existing recording and using it in a new song. Musicians have been sampling for a long time, but the practice has become more common in recent years. Samples from older songs are often used to bring back old memories. ②<u>By using</u> samples that are familiar to older listeners, musicians create music that is popular with people of all ages. Musicians use samples not only ③<u>to bridge</u> generation gaps between listeners, but also to create new approaches to song production. They want to create unique sounds and come up with innovative ways of ④<u>to write</u> songs. Therefore, we can expect to see new and experimental ways of including samples in songs, and for sampling to become more and more popular in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to write → writing: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 ways of writing songs가 맞다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① involves — 주어 'Music sampling(음악 샘플링)'은 단수라서 동사도 단수 involves로 정상이에요.

❌ ② By using — 전치사 By 뒤에 동명사가 온 형태로 'By using(~을 사용함으로써)' 정상이에요.

❌ ③ to bridge — 'not only to bridge(잇기 위해서뿐만 아니라)'에서 목적을 나타내는 to부정사로 정상이에요.

✅ ④ to write — 원문은 writing이에요. 앞에 전치사 of가 있어서 그 뒤에는 동사를 명사처럼 만든 동명사 writing을 써야 해요. 'ways of writing songs(노래를 쓰는 방법)'가 맞고, of 뒤에 to부정사 to write는 쓸 수 없어 틀려요 ←정답
det.tip: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사. of writing(O), of to write(X)

questions.passage: In a scientific study, 72 people were asked to listen to "dad jokes." After each joke, there was either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter. The participants then rated how funny the jokes were. Jokes with no laughter didn't get high ratings. Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated 10 percent funnier. And jokes followed by real laughter were rated 20 percent funnier. This study shows that both real and fake laughter make a big difference in how funny we find jokes. It suggests that we pay close attention not just to a joke's content but also to the reaction it gets. This is because __________ when we hear someone else laughing. Essentially, laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also brings people together. This highlights laughter's social and contagious nature.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 (영어로) 쓰시오.

(다른 사람이 웃는 것을 들으면) 우리는 미소 짓거나 웃을 준비를 하게 된다.
[조건] (1) get, laugh, or, ready, smile, to, we 를 모두 사용 (2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: we get ready to smile or laugh = 우리는 미소 짓거나 웃을 준비를 하게 된다
det.analysis:
주어 we + get ready to(~할 준비가 되다) + 동사원형 smile or laugh. 'This is because ___ when we hear someone else laughing'의 빈칸이에요.

→ get ready to + 동사원형, smile or laugh는 to 뒤에서 등위로 연결 → we get ready to smile or laugh (7단어)
det.tip: get ready to + 동사원형. smile or laugh 순서는 바뀌어도 됨

questions.wa: we get ready to smile or laugh
accept: we get ready to smile or laugh
we get ready to laugh or smile

questions.passage: Music sampling involves taking part of an existing recording and __________. Musicians have been sampling for a long time, but the practice has become more common in recent years. Samples from older songs are often used to bring back old memories. By using samples that are familiar to older listeners, musicians create music that is popular with people of all ages. Musicians use samples not only to bridge generation gaps between listeners, but also to create new approaches to song production. They want to create unique sounds and come up with innovative ways of writing songs. Therefore, we can expect to see new and experimental ways of including samples in songs, and for sampling to become more and more popular in the future.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 영어로 완성하시오.
'그것을 새로운 노래에 사용하는 것'
[조건] (1) a, in, it, new, song, using를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것 (영어로)

det.korean: '그것을 새로운 노래에 사용하는 것' = using it in a new song (6단어)
det.analysis:
'~하는 것'이라 동사를 -ing형으로 시작해요. '사용하다'는 use인데 여기서는 '사용하는 것'이라 using으로 써요.

무엇을 사용하는지는 목적어 it(그것)이에요. use it = 그것을 사용하다.

'새로운 노래에(안에서)'는 전치사 in + a new song이에요. in a new song = 새로운 노래에. 형용사 new가 명사 song을 앞에서 꾸며요.

단어 순서: using → it → in → a → new → song (6단어).
det.tip: using it(그것을 사용하는 것) + in a new song(새로운 노래에)

questions.wa: using it in a new song
accept: using it in a new song

questions.passage: There will soon be many self-driving cars with internet access on the road. Although these cars have many benefits, experts warn that having more self-driving cars also means having more potential targets for hackers. Researchers recently proved through a demonstration that even today's "smart" cars are vulnerable. They used a computer to take control of a car while someone else was driving it. They were not only able to change the radio's volume, adjust the air conditioner, and switch the windshield wipers on, but they were also able to take control of the transmission and stop the car as it was driving down the highway. Fortunately, it was just a demonstration, but it sends a clear message to both the auto industry and the government: __________ that must be taken seriously.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (6단어) (영어로)
'자동차 사이버 보안은 실질적인 문제이다'
[조건] (1) a, automotive, cybersecurity, is, issue, real을 모두 사용할 것
(2) 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: automotive cybersecurity is a real issue = 자동차 사이버 보안은 실질적인 문제이다
det.analysis: 주어(automotive cybersecurity 자동차 사이버 보안) + 동사 is + 보어(a real issue 실질적인 문제) 순서예요. 관사 a는 real issue 앞에 붙여요 → automotive cybersecurity is a real issue
det.tip: 주어 + is + a + 형용사(real) + 명사(issue)

questions.wa: automotive cybersecurity is a real issue
accept: automotive cybersecurity is a real issue

questions.passage: The "sharing economy" is a system based on the idea of individuals renting things from each other through the internet. Things now commonly rented in this way include houses, cars, boats, and power tools. These items are considered by many to be too expensive to own but are owned by others who are willing to share them for a price. This collaborative use of resources has several positive effects. Owners __________, and renters pay less than they would if they bought the things themselves or rented them from a company such as a car rental agency. The environment also benefits because sharing a product with others rather than buying the product for yourself means fewer resources are consumed in making products. As more people use sharing services, these benefits are likely to grow.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (7단어) (영어로)
'그들이 소유한 물건들로 돈을 벌다'
[조건] (1) from, make, money, own, the, they, things를 모두 사용
(2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: make money from the things they own = 그들이 소유한 물건들로 돈을 벌다
det.analysis:
'돈을 벌다'가 핵심이라 make money로 시작해요. '~로부터/~로'는 from the things(그 물건들로), '그들이 소유한'은 관계절 they own이 명사 things를 뒤에서 꾸며요.

make money(돈을 벌다) + from the things(그 물건들로) + they own(그들이 소유한) = make money from the things they own
det.tip: the things they own = 그들이 소유한 물건 (목적격 관계대명사 that 생략)

questions.wa: make money from the things they own
accept: make money from the things they own

questions.passage: Astronauts feel weightless when they travel outside our planet's atmosphere because the speed of a spacecraft in orbit balances the force of Earth's gravitational pull. In fact, you may have experienced a similar feeling when riding a roller coaster. As the roller coaster car climbs up the track, gravity pulls your body downward, and you feel yourself pushed down on your seat. However, when the car rushes down, your body hangs in the air until it is pulled down by your safety belt. Using this phenomenon, NASA __________. The astronauts fly in an aircraft that ascends to an altitude of 24,000 feet, and once the aircraft dives down, the passengers experience about 20 to 25 seconds of weightlessness. These flights help astronauts get used to the environment of space, and they allow NASA to conduct experiments and test equipment in a similar environment as well.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (영어로)
'(NASA는) 자신의 우주비행사들을 우주여행에 대비시킨다'
[조건] (1) astronauts, for, its, prepares, space, travel 를 모두 사용
(2) 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: prepare A for B = A를 B에 대비시키다. NASA가 우주비행사(its astronauts)를 우주여행(space travel)에 대비시켜요.
det.analysis:
본문 문장: 'Using this phenomenon, NASA ______.(이 현상을 이용해 NASA는 ~한다)'

① 동사 prepares(대비시키다)로 시작해요. 주어 NASA가 3인칭 단수라 -s가 붙은 prepares예요.

② 대비시키는 대상은 its astronauts(NASA 자신의 우주비행사들)예요.

③ 'prepare A for B(A를 B에 대비시키다)' 구조에서 B 자리에 for space travel(우주여행을 위해)이 와요.

④ 순서대로 이으면 prepares its astronauts for space travel (6단어)예요.
det.tip: prepare A for B = A를 B에 대비시키다 → prepares its astronauts for space travel.

questions.wa: prepares its astronauts for space travel
accept: prepares its astronauts for space travel
